# qBraid

> Official documentation for qBraid, the quantum computing platform: Lab (cloud IDE), Runtime (SDK, CLI, and REST API), and 20+ QPUs and simulators from 11 providers, unified behind one account and credit system.

> ## Agent Instructions
> Prefer the qBraid CLI for programmatic platform actions: pip install 'qbraid-cli>=0.12', then run `qbraid configure` once with an API key from https://account.qbraid.com/account/api-keys.
> When writing Python, prefer the qBraid SDK: `from qbraid.runtime import QbraidProvider` wraps devices, job submission (`device.run()`), and batch groups (`GroupJobSession`).
> Always install the latest packages (pip install -U qbraid qbraid-cli); do not pin versions from memory. qbraid-cli below 0.12.0 is incompatible with the current API.
> Device IDs use the QRN format vendor:provider:type:name (e.g. qbraid:qbraid:sim:qir-sv, rigetti:rigetti:qpu:cepheus-1-108q). Legacy underscore IDs are deprecated.
> The REST API base URL is https://api-v2.qbraid.com/api/v1, authenticated with an X-API-Key header.
> For endpoints without a dedicated wrapper, use `QbraidSessionV1` from `qbraid_core` — an authenticated session (`.get()`/`.post()`) that sets the X-API-Key header. Full spec: https://docs.qbraid.com/openapi-v2.json
> Free simulators cost no credits; QPU and GPU jobs consume credits. Surface the estimated cost to the user before submitting a paid job.
> For account signup, API keys, credits, and end-to-end action recipes, see https://qbraid.com/llms.txt.

- [Writing a New Provider](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/runtime/new-provider.md): A step-by-step guide to implementing a new provider class.
- [Run on qBraid](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/getting-started.md): Submit to every quantum device and simulator on qBraid with one qBraid API key, using the QbraidProvider.
- [Managing jobs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/managing-jobs.md): Estimate what a job will cost, label and track it, read its cost and timing, see what ran on the device, and reconnect to it later.
- [Batch and group jobs](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/jobs.md): Run several circuits through the QbraidProvider as separate jobs, as one batch job on one device, or as a group of jobs across devices.
- [Device calibrations and connectivity](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/calibrations.md): Fetch live coupling maps and calibration data for QPUs on qBraid, plot connectivity graphs, and use the data to place circuits on the best-calibrated qubits before submitting.
- [AQT](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/aqt.md): Run on Alpine Quantum Technologies' IBEX Q1 trapped-ion QPU through qBraid, with only a qBraid API key.
- [GPU simulators](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/gpu-simulators.md): Running circuits on qBraid's GPU state-vector and tensor-network simulators through the QbraidProvider, with every option, their limits, daily allowance, and per-minute pricing.
- [IonQ](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/ionq.md): Run on IonQ's Forte trapped-ion QPUs and the IonQ simulator through qBraid, with only a qBraid API key.
- [IQM](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/iqm.md): Run on IQM's Garnet and Emerald superconducting QPUs through qBraid, with only a qBraid API key.
- [Quobly Alloy Forge](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/quobly.md): Running circuits against Quobly's silicon spin-qubit emulator through the QbraidProvider, with and without the Pioneer hardware noise model.
- [QuEra](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/quera.md): Run analog Hamiltonian simulation programs on QuEra's Aquila neutral-atom QPU through qBraid, with only a qBraid API key.
- [Rigetti](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/rigetti.md): Run gate-model and timing-aware programs on Rigetti's Cepheus-1-108Q through qBraid, with only a qBraid API key and from any qBraid-supported framework.
- [Amazon Braket](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/aws.md): The Amazon Braket submission path: how compilation, qubit placement, bit ordering, and Braket runtime options work for every aws:* device on qBraid, plus Braket's SV1 and DM1 simulators.
- [Open Quantum](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/open-quantum.md): How devices with openquantum: IDs work through qBraid: linking an Open Quantum account, how jobs are billed, and what they accept.
- [Self-managed providers](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/self-managed.md): Use the qBraid SDK with your own account and credentials at a quantum vendor or cloud. Jobs, billing, and keys are between you and the vendor.
- [Amazon Braket (self-managed)](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/self-managed/aws.md): Run on Amazon Braket devices with your own AWS account, using the BraketProvider.
- [AQT (self-managed)](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/self-managed/aqt.md): Run on AQT trapped-ion quantum processors with your own AQT arnica account, using the AQTProvider.
- [Azure Quantum (self-managed)](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/self-managed/azure.md): Run on Azure Quantum devices with your own Azure Quantum workspace, using the AzureQuantumProvider.

- [IonQ (self-managed)](https://docs.qbraid.com/v2/sdk/user-guide/providers/self-managed/ionq.md): Run on IonQ simulators and QPUs with your own IonQ API key, using the IonQProvider.
